purpose: 为VesselForge/PG-Frag/A12到RelicWeave的碎片到历史邻片候选服务提供可核对的对象级参考；不作为完整历史真实性或复原认证数据集。

evidence_contract.FACT_FROM_SOURCE: 藏品页直接记载的名称、年代、地域、材料、工艺、尺寸、纹饰和制作描述。
evidence_contract.VISUAL_INFERENCE: 由来源尺寸做的粗比例计算或受馆藏照片视角限制的宽泛外观判断；不等同于测量。
evidence_contract.GENERATOR_SUGGESTION: 面向检索或参数化生成的建议，不是关于原器的事实。
evidence_contract.UNKNOWN: 所查记录未提供，保持未知；不得由单张照片估算精确壁厚、曲率、表面法向或力学参数。

source_method.source_type: The Metropolitan Museum of Art official collection records
source_method.open_access_status: Each object page displays a Public Domain label and states that Open Access data and public-domain images are available for unrestricted commercial and noncommercial use without permission or fee.
source_method.image_handling: No image, CAD, scan, or derivative mesh was downloaded or embedded. Image-entry counts are page metadata only; no calibrated orthographic coverage is claimed.
source_method.materials_literature: No object-specific material paper was used because these collection pages provide no matching laboratory measurements. General ceramics properties were not imputed to individual objects.

fact_from_source: Title Bowl; early 11th century; attributed to Egypt.
Earthenware; luster-painted; height 6.7 cm; diameter 24.9 cm.
The curatorial text mentions Fatimid luster painting and Abbasid scroll-and-dot decoration.
visual_inference: Reported height divided by diameter is approximately 0.27, a coarse shallow-envelope clue only; it is not a profile measurement.
Still photographs do not establish exact color, reflectance, luster thickness, or calibrated curvature.
generator_suggestion: Use as a shallow-bowl candidate with a source-linked luster-painted/scroll/dot surface vocabulary.
Keep shape and decoration confidence separate; pattern evidence alone does not establish the historical vessel family.
unknowns: Wall thickness, foot/base profile, full inside/outside contour, local curvature, composition, firing conditions, strength, and instrument-measured color/gloss.

fact_from_source: Title Beaker; Neolithic Longshan culture; China.
Burnished black earthenware; height 18.6 cm; top diameter 14.9 cm.
visual_inference: Height divided by top diameter is approximately 1.25, so the listed vertical extent exceeds the opening width; no side profile follows from this ratio.
Black and burnished are curatorial material terms, not measured RGB, reflectance, or roughness.
generator_suggestion: Store height and top diameter as a coarse envelope for a beaker candidate; keep burnished-black surface metadata separate.
Do not interpolate a foot or wall profile from only these two dimensions.
unknowns: Rim section, bottom dimensions, complete profile, wall thickness, clay composition, firing conditions, roughness, gloss, and mechanical properties.

fact_from_source: Title Jar; Late Jōmon; Japan; earthenware with incised decoration.
Curatorial text describes bulbous body, narrow neck, incised decoration, red pigment, two sets of suspension apertures, and qualitatively thin walls.
visual_inference: The words bulbous and narrow-neck are curatorial descriptions, not a digitized curve.
Red is a curatorial pigment description, not a calibrated photo color.
generator_suggestion: Expose bulbous body, narrow neck, paired aperture zones, and incised-surface tags as separately selectable candidate features.
Treat thin-wall wording as qualitative only; never emit a millimeter value without measurement.
unknowns: Numerical wall thickness, neck opening, aperture diameter/coordinates, base diameter, full profile, incision spacing/depth, pigment/clay composition, firing settings, and mechanical properties.

decoration_and_surface_evidence: The body is cast from two hemispherical molds stamped with impressions; the impressions create raised repeating patterns.
The halves are joined using wet clay; a smoothed clay band visibly marks the center join.
The neck and handle are wheel-thrown and attached after joining the molded body.
The record does not describe spout geometry.

color_evidence.source_wording: The record describes unglazed earthenware but does not name a body color.
color_evidence.photo_only_color_claim: No precise hue or reflectance is recorded.

fact_from_source: Title Ewer; 12th–13th century; excavated in Nishapur, Iran.
Earthenware; molded decoration, unglazed; height 27.9 cm; one diameter 14.6 cm with location unspecified.
Curatorial text details the molded two-part body, raised repeated impressions, joined seam, separately wheel-thrown neck, and handle.
visual_inference: The source describes a visible smoothed central seam; seam relief size and mold pattern depth remain unmeasured.
The listed diameter's measurement location is unspecified, so it does not define the body or rim profile.
generator_suggestion: Consider a handled ewer/pitcher candidate branch when shard evidence supports a neck, handle, or pouring form.
Represent molded relief and construction seam as separate optional evidence-backed features.
Do not invent a spout contour from the title alone.
unknowns: Spout form, handle section, complete body curve, diameter location, seam thickness, relief height/pitch, wall thickness, clay composition, firing conditions, and mechanical properties.

generator_suggestion: Keep black decoration and turquoise glaze as separate source-linked surface-layer candidates.

unknowns: Motif content/position, glaze thickness, rim/base dimensions, complete contour, wall thickness, material chemistry, firing conditions, calibrated color, and mechanical properties.

cross_record_generator_rules: Bowl, beaker, and jar are retrieval candidates, not historical-identity labels.
Separate morphology, manufacture/decoration technique, and finish/color into distinct evidence fields.
Preserve source record identifiers on every suggested feature; retain UNKNOWN for unsupported dimensions.
Do not infer exact thickness, curvature, surface normals, material chemistry, or mechanical properties from still photographs.
Only suggest historical motifs when fragment or query evidence supports them; do not blend regional styles into an unverified composite.
missing_evidence_for_higher_fidelity: Calibrated multi-view photography or a museum/archaeology photogrammetry or structured-light mesh with scale, coordinate system, registration, and damage masks.
Cross-section or CT data for wall thickness and interior/exterior constraints.
Object-specific material analyses or laboratory reports for composition, glaze thickness, porosity, elastic modulus, flexural strength, or fracture toughness.
